schema: llm-sizer/factors v1 — derived by scripts/llm-sizer/calibrate.py from benchmarks.json; do not edit by hand

efficiency._formula: decode tok/s = bandwidth_gbs × efficiency ÷ gigabytes read per token (active weights at the quant's bits + context cache per token)
efficiency._resolve: exact chip if present in by_chip, else assumed[chip] if present, else the tier median (tier from the chip name: base | Pro | Max | Ultra; DGX Spark = spark)

M5 Ultra.note: ultra-tier median 0.438 × M5 generation lift 1.265 (M5 Max vs M4 Max); replace when measured; fixed-cost model: unmeasured: 85 % of spec bandwidth (the Ultra tier's share) and the M5 generation's fixed cost; replace when measured

gguf.note: llama.cpp / LM Studio GGUF is the baseline

mlx.note: 2026 community MLX-vs-llama.cpp reports; applied in full up to 24K context and fading linearly to 1.0 at 36K

speed_model._formula: ms per token = GB read per token ÷ (b_eff_ratio × spec bandwidth) × 1000 × read_factor[quant family] (the K-quant factor on the platforms it lists: Apple silicon) + (t0_ms + architecture_cost_ms[class]) × mlx overhead_factor[group] (GGUF: 1); on MLX a mixture under 6B active instead + expert layers × mlx expert_layer.ms_per_layer[chip generation; one without rows takes the previous generation's] + (attention_ms_per_32k[attention] + mlx attention_ms_per_32k[chip generation: pre_m5 | m5plus]) × attended ÷ 32768 + mlx index_ms_per_32k[chip generation] × context ÷ 32768 (sparse-attention models on MLX); tok/s = 1000 ÷ ms. attended = the context, or a sparse-attention model's budget on MLX (constants.ts:SPARSE_ATTENTION, 2,048 for Flash Next); the cache in GB read per token counts the attended tokens
speed_model._classes: dense | moe (mixture of experts) | moe_hybrid (mixture of experts with linear-attention layers) | moe_latent (mixture of experts with MLA or latent attention) | deepseek_v4 (per-model override) | flash_next (the n-gram-table architecture, Qwen 3.8 Flash Next)
speed_model._groups: MLX overhead groups: dense | small_active_moe_m4plus (under 6B active, M4 generation and newer) | small_active_moe_pre_m4 | moe_other; the two small_active groups take the expert-layer rule wherever the model has a layer count, and their overhead factors only where it has none. MLX context-cost groups: pre_m5 (M1 to M4, and any chip whose generation is not known) | m5plus (M5 and newer)

pre_m5.note: no sparse-attention MLX row past 8K on this generation; the m5plus value × 9.00, the ratio of the two generations' MLX attention costs

validation.holdout_rule: family == gemma-4, or contributor == omlx with no row past 8K, by submission_id; the two oMLX M5 Max submissions that run past 8K (Qwen 3.8 27B to 64K, Nemotron 3 Super at 32K) train the M5-generation MLX context cost, the only long-context M5 rows there are; since 0.16 the oMLX community rows (contributor omlx-community, 2026-10) train on the chips of the 128 GB comparison (M5 Max, M4 Max, M2 Ultra) and hold out on the others (M5 Pro, M3 Ultra, the 64-core M1 Ultra, M5 Ultra), whole submissions; the 48-core M1 Ultra and the one plain M5 Ultra Flash Next session are report rows; since 0.17 the oMLX community rows scraped on 2026-10-19 (one row per model, chip and GPU bin, the median of the plain sessions within 10 % of that group's median, every run id in the note; a group validation.json already covers at 4K is not added) train on gpt-oss-20b, gpt-oss-120b and Qwen3-Coder-Next and hold out whole families, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Gemma 4, and every M5 Ultra row

acceleration._rule: MTP: native heads, factor in [min, max] when the runtime uses them. Draft models (DFlash/DSpark): use draft_dense unless the model is a mixture-of-experts with under 6.0 B active parameters, then draft_small_active_moe. Always show the range, never the headline.

prefill._formula: prefill tok/s at a short prompt = K ÷ active parameters (B), K = per_core[generation] × GPU cores (Apple) or by_chip (others), × kquant for K-quant and IQ GGUF files, × class[arch], × mlx[generation group] on MLX; rate at context depth d = short-prompt rate ÷ (1 + d ÷ D0), D0 = context.by_model[model][runtime] where a model has its own sweep, else (context.d0_tokens on GGUF, context.mlx.d0_tokens on MLX) × attention_share_ref ÷ the model's share of attention layers; wait before the first word for an n-token prompt = (n + n² ÷ (2 × D0)) ÷ short-prompt rate

_excluded.note: MLX rows measured at a prompt shorter than this carry the per-request start-up cost and do not set the MLX factor

context.note: D0 is the context depth at which the reading rate has halved, fitted per runtime on the measured ladders (llama.cpp: d0_tokens, n_points = ladders; MLX: mlx), for a model with attention in a quarter of its layers; other models scale D0 by their share of full-attention layers (assumed); a model with a published depth sweep of its own takes its own value on that runtime (by_model)

cluster._formula: layer split: ms per token = one machine's ms for the whole model + hop_ms[link] × (machines − 1); tensor parallel: ms = one machine's ms ÷ machines + tensor_c_ms[class] × log2(machines); reading speed × prefill.layer_factor on a layer split, × machines ^ prefill.tensor_exponent under tensor parallel
cluster._links: hop_ms and the gpu tensor constant are keyed by link class: mac (Thunderbolt 5) | spark (the 200 Gb/s ports of a DGX Spark or GX10) | gpu (cards on PCIe inside one box)

gpu.note: assumed: no published layer-split series across several cards in one box; PCIe 5 is faster than either measured link, so the hop is set below both
assumed: one MiniMax-M2.5 pair on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell cards over PCIe 5 implies roughly this, and its quant changes with the card count, so it is quoted and not fitted

layer_factor.note: assumed flat: only one layer-split series publishes prompt reading at two machine counts (llama.cpp RPC on two DGX Sparks, pp2048 389.5 tok/s on one machine and 453.9 on two, 1.17 times), so reading speed stays flat until a second series exists

tensor_exponent.note: assumed: tensor parallel divides the prompt work, so reading should scale with the count, but only one short-prompt point exists (vLLM on DGX Sparks, time to first word 233 ms on one machine and 149 ms on two, 1.56 times); machines ^ 0.75 gives 1.68 at two machines, a little above that point

dispatch_caveat.note: a very deep mixture of experts can be dispatch-bound under tensor parallel: Kimi-K3 2.78T on four Mac Studio M3 Ultra wrote 2 tok/s where the bandwidth maths says about 36, because per-kernel dispatch overhead dominates on 92 layers with top-16 routing; above this layer count the tool warns instead of promising the number
